title: Fork lifted intent and continue safely
description: Prototype fork workflows at the lifted prompt's exact boundary. Compare run-versus-seed behavior and source-versus-fork background continuation, including no marker, '.', '(Continue)', and a future structured continuation fact.
acceptance_criteria: A user can create a provenance-linked fork at the correct boundary, choose whether the lifted prompt is seeded or submitted, choose which branch runs, and recover from partial failure without duplicate execution; marker effects on model context are documented.
notes:
Implementing first TUI prototype for seed-dormant-topic and run-fork/defer-source workflows using public V2 client operations. Composer injection is not public; prototype will represent a seed as queued pending input with resume:false.
Prototype implemented and verified: /dance-seed creates a provenance-linked fork with a queued resume:false seed; /dance-fork queues optional source continuation, runs selected prompt in fork, and lets user focus source or fork. Effect workflows retry prompt admission once with stable IDs, preserve projected attachment bytes, and guard staged source reverts. 13 tests plus type/lint/build pass. Remaining acceptance gaps: public TUI composer injection, ambiguous fork-creation reconciliation/idempotency, lifted-prompt persistence, and broader source-vs-fork execution permutations.

title: Persist lifted prompts with transcript provenance
description: Define Ctrl-X U as a recoverable prompt-lifting operation. Preserve prompt text and attachments, source Session, message or transcript boundary, timestamps, replacement policy, and later restore/fork disposition across TUI restarts.
acceptance_criteria: A lifted prompt survives restart, restores safely into the composer, retains source and boundary metadata, distinguishes editor/pending/promoted/executing states, and cannot be silently lost or duplicated.

title: Make interruption recoverable and branchable
description: Give long-running OpenCode sessions deliberate cadence: persist lifted prompts with transcript provenance, create explicit check-in boundaries, and turn redirected intent into safe named forks. The epic preserves open product choices around transcript replacement markers and foreground/background execution.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed design defines lifted-prompt lifecycle, check-in semantics, fork behavior, persistence ownership, required OpenCode seams, and the dependency on fork-aware retitling; implementation children can proceed independently without losing prompt text or provenance.

title: Name cadence-created forks
description: Give cadence-created forks useful literal or generated titles. Coordinate with https://github.com/rektide/opencode-retitle and its fork-provenance model; record any required OpenCode V2 title-mutation or action/command seam rather than building a competing title system.
acceptance_criteria: Fork creation accepts a literal title without model generation; generated naming can use source title, lifted prompt, last shared work, and first divergence; retitling failure never blocks fork creation; required upstream/plugin seams and related project dependencies are explicit.

title: Define explicit and automatic check-ins
description: Add a deliberate conversational boundary that can pause for review, redirect, fork, continue, or stop with a handoff. Begin with explicit invocation and one conservative safe-boundary trigger before adaptive policy.
acceptance_criteria: The design distinguishes model-visible transcript content from UI/plugin state, specifies suppression and snoozing, identifies safe trigger boundaries, and proves an explicit check-in without ceremonial or repeated interruption.
